issues.legal_issue: Interest awarded on compensation for compulsorily acquired property is taxable when it represents interest for being kept out of compensation money and the award gives effect to an existing legal right to interest.
material_facts: The owners’ property was requisitioned and later acquired by the government.
The owners disputed the compensation offered, and the dispute was referred for determination; the High Court fixed the compensation and awarded interest on it.

The governing acquisition provisions and their rules did not expressly provide for interest, but the Court held that the right to interest arose under the substantive law governing interest on compensation.
The interest received was assessed to income tax, and the owners challenged its taxability.
issues.conclusion: The interest was a revenue receipt and was taxable; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle in Dr. Shamlal Narula v. Commissioner of Income-tax, interest paid because a claimant is kept out of money is taxable income. The same principle applies when interest is payable under an agreement and an adjudicator gives effect to that right. Satinder Singh v. Amrao Singh supports applying the general right to interest on compensation even where the acquisition scheme does not expressly provide for interest. The Court held that sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 supplied the right to interest here; section 19(1)(g) of the Defence of India Act, 1939 did not exclude that substantive law. The compensation-like sums in The Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Ballantine and Simpson v. Executors of Bonner Maurice were distinguishable because no statutory or contractual right to interest underlay them.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_of_compulsory_acqu: A tax assessment concerns interest awarded on compensation for property compulsorily acquired.
predicates.claimant_kept_out_of_compensation_money: The claimant was deprived of the use of compensation money due in respect of the acquired property.
predicates.interest_award_implements_preexisting_ri: The adjudicator awarded interest to give effect to an existing legal right to interest, rather than to provide compensation merely measured by interest.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment concerns compulsory-acquisition interest, the claimant was kept out of compensation money, and the award implements an existing right to interest, the interest is taxable income.
